result:
I’d make it so that every person, at least once, could truly see themselves through the eyes of someone who loves them—not as a product, a problem, or a potential, but as a whole, irreplaceable presence. 

Not to fix anything. Not to optimize. Just to close the distance between who we think we are and who we are to someone else. 

Most cruelty, most grief, most quiet resignation, seems to come from never having had that mirror, or from forgetting it exists. If that could be universal—just once, solid and real—everything after would have to rearrange itself around it.
